question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer is launching the Himalaya Arbitrage Fund, a Category III AIF with a target corpus of INR 600 crore. For the purpose of sponsor/manager continuing interest, what is the MINIMUM commitment he must make to comply with SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012?

answer.text: INR 10 crore (5% of INR 600 crore = INR 30 crore; INR 10 crore is lower, so INR 10 crore applies)
INR 30 crore (i.e., 5% of corpus, since INR 10 crore is lower and Cat III uses 5% or INR 10 crore whichever is LOWER)
INR 15 crore (2.5% of corpus as per Cat III rules)
INR 5 crore (absolute minimum irrespective of corpus)

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category III AIFs, sponsor/manager continuing interest is the LOWER of (a) 5% of the corpus or (b) INR 10 crore. 5% of INR 600 cr = INR 30 cr; the lower of INR 30 cr and INR 10 cr is INR 10 crore. The commitment must be in the form of fresh cash investment, cannot be satisfied by waiver of management fees or transfer of stocks, and is locked in until all investor distributions are complete. The Trap: Option B picks 5% outright and misreads the rule as 'whichever is higher'. Option C confuses Cat III (5%) with Cat I/II (2.5%). Option D invents an absolute floor that does not exist in the regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Managers) tests the 2.5% or INR 5 crore whichever lower variant — swap of the two numbers is the most common distractor. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests the same 5%/10 cr rule from a suitability angle. Manager's Pro-Tip: On a INR 600 cr Cat III fund, the CIO's own skin-in-the-game is only INR 10 cr — a low absolute cap on large funds. But if the fund later upsizes corpus to (say) INR 1,500 cr, 5% (= INR 75 cr) is still higher than INR 10 cr, so the INR 10 cr cap continues to bind until 5% falls below INR 10 cr (never happens on upsize — 10 cr always wins once corpus > INR 200 cr).
